title: Counting the Months of a Disability Compensation Dependency Release Against Issued and Returned Payments
content:
**Rule.** The months a Disability Compensation dependency release covers depend on how the claims' effective date compares with the monthly payments the award has issued, and on whether any monthly payment came back:

| The claims' effective date | A monthly payment came back | Months covered |
|---|---|---|
| Lies further back than the number of monthly payments the award has issued | Yes | The monthly payments issued, less one for each monthly payment that came back |
| Lies further back than the number of monthly payments the award has issued | No | The monthly payments issued |
| Lies within the months the award has paid | Yes | The whole months elapsed from the claims' effective date to the issue date of the most recent monthly payment, less one for each monthly payment that came back |
| Lies within the months the award has paid | No | Those whole months |

**Terms.** The effective date "lies further back than the number of monthly payments the award has issued" when the whole months elapsed from it to the issue date of the most recent monthly payment are more than the count of monthly payments on the award; otherwise it lies within the months the award has paid. The monthly payments issued are the monthly payment entries in the award's payment history; a monthly payment that came back is one with a returned-payment entry.

**Worked cases (hypothetical; the issue date of the most recent monthly payment is 1 March 2026)**

1. Effective date 14 June 2025 (8 whole months); the award has issued 5 monthly payments and 1 came back. The 8 months are more than the 5 payments, so the release covers 5 less 1, that is 4 months.
2. Same, with no payment returned: 5 months.
3. Effective date 14 June 2025 (8 whole months); the award has issued 12 monthly payments and 2 came back. The 8 months lie within the months paid, so the release covers 8 less 2, that is 6 months.
4. Same, with no payment returned: 8 months.
5. Boundary: 8 whole months and exactly 8 monthly payments issued, none returned. The months are not more than the payments, so the release covers the 8 whole months.
